processing: Black tea, fully oxidised and made in the company's own factories in the highlands. Grade-by-grade methods are little documented.
harvest_season: Little is documented on prized pickings; the tea is sold as a year-round product and no single season defines it.
appearance_dry: Dark, fine leaf, as is usual for a large-scale packaged black tea.
appearance_liquor: Clear reddish amber, typical of a highland black tea.
appearance_wet: Small coppery-brown leaf, as expected of this type.
taste_profile: Independent tasting records are thin; expect the clean, fairly light highland black tea usual for the Cameron Highlands, with enough briskness to take milk.

brewing.notes: A general starting point for a small-leaf black tea. Good plain or with milk; shorten the steep if it turns sharp.

vintage_note: Sold year-round as a packaged brand tea, with no vintage or season on the pack. Treat it as an everyday tea: buy by the best-before date and drink it fresh.
description:
BOH is Malaysia's largest black tea maker and its plantation in the Cameron Highlands is the largest in the country. For most Malaysians, this simply is tea.

The leaf comes from highland gardens and goes through the company's own factories. The company publishes little on grade-by-grade methods, so it is best taken as a modern industrial black tea.

In the cup, expect what is usual for the highlands: clean, fairly light and brisk enough for milk. Brew it hot and short, and do not expect it to re-steep like a whole-leaf tea.

It is easy to find and honestly priced, with no vintages to decode. If you are in the highlands, the Sungei Palas garden near Tringkap has a visitor centre and cafe overlooking the slopes.
history:
J. A. Russell, a British-born businessman, founded BOH in 1929 during the colonial period in Malaya. It was the first hill-country estate in the territory.

A 2024 report lists three highland gardens: Boh, Fairlie and Sungei Palas.
